subject: Bridging latency blips to QBR asks — postmortem & action lattice
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Analytics <support@acme-analytics.com>, Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Bridging latency blips to QBR asks — postmortem & action lattice

Team — sending a concise postmortem and the set of direct asks we should carry into the QBR deck for Acme (and the leadership readout). TL;DR: a regression in batching policy + a kernel fallback path introduced by the 2028-08-10 runtime roll caused intermittent 95th/99th percentile token latency spikes for ~90 minutes on 2028-08-14, impacting ~12 active sessions for Acme. Customer-facing impact: brief timeouts during long-run prompt streams; no data leakage, no model corruption.

Timeline (high-level):
- 2028-08-14 17:05 UTC: Observability alert — 95th token latency > 2.5s
- 17:07 UTC: Auto-fallback to smaller batch size triggered; some nodes hit kernel fallback leading to temporary cold-path slows
- 17:23 UTC: Mitigation — revert batching override and hotpatch kernel selection (hotfix v2028.08.14a)
- 18:40 UTC: Metrics back to baseline; post-incident sweeps started

Root cause (short): regression in heuristic that chooses batch-size threshold for mixed-length streams; combined with rare kernel selector mismatch for that model variant on 80GB A100 nodes. We have a reproducible test-case (attached log extract) and an actionable fix.

Impact summary:
- Customers affected: 12 sessions for Acme; estimated error/timeout rate ~1.1% of token requests in window
- SLA: We breached the 99.9% token success percent for a rolling hour; legal/finance will need to confirm exact credit.

Immediate mitigations already taken:
1) Hotfix v2028.08.14a reverted the batching heuristic change (complete).
2) Forced kernel pinning on affected pools until selector fix (complete).
3) Created load-suppress policy for mixed-length streams in routing (in progress).

Concrete action items (owners & due dates):
- ACTION-01: Kernel selector unit tests + deploy to staging (owner: Marissa Cole) — due 2028-08-18
- ACTION-02: Permanent config rollback + canary of revised batching heuristic (owner: Hannah Schmitt) — due 2028-08-20
- ACTION-03: Customer communication + credit calc proposal (owner: Jordan Blake) — draft due 2028-08-16; final by 2028-08-17
- ACTION-04: Runbook update for mixed-length stream detection + alert tuning (owner: Marissa Cole) — due 2028-08-19 (patch attached)

QBR asks (what I want leadership to fold into the QBR slide set):
- A one-slide incident summary (impact, timeline, RCA, next milestones) — Vivek: can you sign off on the final 1-slide wording?
- Approval for a customer goodwill credit up to $12,000 (prelim calc attached) — Evelyn: legal/finance check?
- Commitment to an SRE + Runtime paired drill in Sept to validate rolling fixes (owner: Vivek)

Attachments: postmortem-slide-deck.pdf (working slides), acme_incident_log_extract.csv (repro logs), runbook-update-diff.patch (proposed runbook changes).

I'll consolidate edits into the slide deck if you send me inline comments. Need sign-off for the customer credit ask by EOD 2028-08-17 so we can finalize QBR materials.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Aug 2028 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Bridging latency blips to QBR asks — postmortem & action lattice

Jordan — thanks for the clear write-up. Two quick things:
1) Please distill this to a single slide (one metric snapshot + one-line RCA + three next steps) by EOD tomorrow. I want leadership to consume a single visual in the QBR.
2) For the customer credit ask: can you provide a short justification (methodology: hours impacted x average per-hour revenue, plus goodwill factor) and a recommended figure? Evelyn can sign off after finance/legal review.

I'll take ownership of the Sept drill and will coordinate with SRE/Runtime. Marissa/Hannah — please make the test-case reproducible in CI and include a perf baseline before/after.

Vivek
SVP, Engineering
Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 15 Aug 2028 13:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Bridging latency blips to QBR asks — postmortem & action lattice

Jordan — quick finance/legal checklist from my side:
- Confirmed we hit the SLA window; need legal to confirm the precise credit calculation approach.
- Please split the "credit recommendation" into: 1) contractual credit (formula-based) and 2) goodwill (discretionary). Keep them separate in the slide.
- If the contractual credit exceeds $8k, I need Finance to pre-approve; otherwise I can approve as part of standard goodwill up to $8k.

Marissa/Hannah — when you update the runbook, flag any alerts that are noisy vs. true regressions so we can tighten incident-assignment thresholds for QBR dashboards.

Evelyn Hart
VP, Finance & Ops
Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 15 Aug 2028 17:22:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Bridging latency blips to QBR asks — postmortem & action lattice

Jordan — appreciate the rapid follow-up and the hotfix. For context from our side: we saw intermittent timeouts during two long-running inference tasks (one batch ETL job and one streaming inference session). The ETL job retried and completed; the streaming session dropped frames for ~90 seconds which impacted a demo to our internal stakeholders.

We would like:
- A formal incident summary we can share internally (one page)
- Confirmation of the proposed remediation timeline
- The proposed credit figure and a short explanation we can forward to procurement

Thanks for looping us in; we'll plan to discuss briefly during the QBR.

Best,
Elena Rossi
Head of ML Engineering
Acme Analytics

- Canary plan for revised batching heuristic: staging canary tomorrow (2028-08-16), roll to 10% production on 2028-08-17 if green.
